newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Bank of Tallinn mulls expansion into Latvia.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Tallinn mulls expansion into Latvia.

text.p: Estonia's Bank of Tallinn said on Wednesday it planned to open a financial service firm in the Latvian capital, Riga, and would then consider setting up a branch in its southern neighbour.
"In the near future, we will open a financial service firm in Riga," Rait Lukas, chairman of Bank of Tallinn's board, told Reuters.
"We are carefully examining the markets in the other Baltic states and western Russia," Lukas said, adding that the bank was mulling the idea of establishing a branch office in Latvia.
"We will be present in Latvia, gaining first-hand experience before further (expasnion) decisions are made."
Estonia's largest bank, Hansa Bank, moved into the Latvian market ealier this year when it acquired the German-Latvian bank.
Latvia is still recovering from a crisis which rocked its banking sector last year when the largest bank in the Baltic states, Banka Baltiya, was shut.
The Bank of Tallinn, which is quoted on the local bourse, is the fourth largest in Estonia with assets worth 1.5 billion kroons.
